corrections.ordered_by: "i want the same methods for them, embeddings via gpu, etc etc.." (2026-10-27) · "ffs, redo them on the gpu" · "only the embeddings, because i want the true times" (2026-10-25, on the final runs' query embeddings made on the CPU)
corrections.what_happened: The run embedded queries on the graphics card while other questions of the run were under way. Each question's query-embedding time is the time the same embeddings take on the desktop's GTX 1080 Ti one call after the other, as for the runs on the hundred.

rule.text:
1. An embed call record that says device cpu is corrected; with --all, every embed call record,
     also one made on the graphics card while other questions of the run were under way. The
     evidence file names, per question, exactly the records of rule 1, by their seq.
  2. Each question with such records gets in its embed entry in retrieval request_s = the GPU
     seconds of its embed calls added, and time_s = request_s + wait_s + retry_s; wait_s and
     retry_s stay as recorded.
  3. The question's timing.wall_s changes by the same amount as the embed entry's request_s.
  4. Each record of rule 1 gets its GPU seconds as encode_s and device cuda. No vector, answer,
     context, score or other time changes; the vectors are the same (cosine checked).

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: The GPU times were measured one call after the other in a warm process; the lock waits of the run (wait_s) stay as recorded.

evidence.what: per question, each embed call's GPU seconds and, where the run kept the CPU vector, the cosine of its vector to it
